extracted.intended_audience: prospective Guggenheim applicants (artists, scholars, scientists) and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for eligibility, selection, and application materials for the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation fellowships, aimed at mid-career artists and scholars. Covers who may apply, what the foundation values (past accomplishment and future promise), required materials, award use, and how grant amounts are determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated distinguished accomplishment and potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are bestowed upon individuals who have demonstrated distinguished accomplishment in the past and potential for future achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core selection criterion: evidence of a significant prior record combined with promise of future work. The Foundation rewards both accomplished track records and indications of future productivity or impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding aptitude for prolific scholarship or exceptional artistic talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients exhibit outstanding aptitude for prolific scholarship or exceptional talent in the arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors applicants who have shown either high scholarly productivity or exceptional artistic ability. Emphasis may differ by discipline, but both scholarship and artistic excellence are recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field eligibility (disciplines covered)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation awards fellowships to professionals in the natural sciences, social sciences, humanities, and the creative arts, excluding the performing arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should come from these fields; the performing arts are generally excluded though some related practitioners (see exclusions/allowances) remain eligible. The Foundation treats a wide range of scholarly and creative disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performing arts exclusions and specific allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: The performing arts are excluded from these fellowships, but composers, film directors, and choreographers are still eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the general rule excludes performing performers, certain creative roles connected to performance (composition, film directing, choreography) are explicitly eligible. Check discipline-specific guidance when borderline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-stage eligibility (mid-career professionals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students are not qualified to apply; advanced professionals in mid-career, such as published authors, are encouraged to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fellowship targets established practitioners rather than students or early-career trainees. Applicants should demonstrate an advanced/professional standing and a body of work consistent with mid-career status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic/competition eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation holds two separate competitions each year: one open to citizens and permanent residents of the United States and Canada; the other to citizens and permanent residents of Latin America and the Caribbean (the Latin America and Caribbean competition is currently suspended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must apply to the competition appropriate to their citizenship/permanent residency. Note current suspension of the Latin America and Caribbean competition — check Foundation announcements for status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are required to submit references as well as a CV and portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a strong CV, supporting portfolio (creative work, publications, etc.), and references/recommendation letters. These materials provide the primary evidence of past accomplishment and potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and duration adjustments based on individual needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The size of each grant varies and the amount and duration of the grant is adjusted based on the individual needs of the recipients, taking into consideration their other resources and the purpose and scope of their plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant budgets are individualized: propose a realistic plan and budget that reflect what you need to accomplish the project. The Foundation considers applicants' other funding/resources and the project's scope when setting award size and term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended purpose of the fellowship (time and freedom to pursue projects)
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of the grant is to provide recipients with dedicated time and freedom to pursue their projects or artistic endeavours, while being relieved of their regular duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should make clear how the fellowship period will enable significant progress or creative work by freeing the applicant from usual obligations. The Foundation expects the fellowship to facilitate meaningful work rather than routine duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of funds by Fellows
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of the grant, Fellows are free to use the funds however they deem fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though budgets are considered when awarding, Fellows are ultimately given latitude in using funds; applicants should nevertheless explain intended use to justify requested award size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity/competitiveness (approximate award statistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year the foundation receives between 500 and 4,000 applications and awards approximately 175 Fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fellowship is competitive; applicants should present strong evidence of prior achievement and a compelling plan to stand out among many applicants.
